_comments.add_district: Add an object to the 'districts' array with id, name, description, color (one of: blood, teal, gold, purple, slate)
_comments.add_location: Add an object to 'locations' with a unique id, number, districtId matching a district id, x/y as % coordinates (x=0 is left, x=100 is right, y=0 is top, y=100 is bottom), unlockPhase matching a phase id, and a detailsByPhase block
_comments.add_phase: Add to town.phases with a new id and the next order number. Then add matching keys to each location's detailsByPhase
_comments.move_marker: Change the x and y values on a location. Open the map image, find the spot visually, and estimate as a percentage of image width/height
_comments.add_secret: Add to a location's secrets array with unlockPhase set to the phase when it becomes visible to players

districts.name: Civic Quarter
districts.description: The administrative heart of Dunmore — the roundabout plaza, the town hall, official buildings. The seat of what passes for order in a city on the edge of something ugly.

districts.name: High Quarter
districts.description: Dunmore's small upper class lives here — old stone manors, private gardens, a deliberate remove from the noise of the lower city. Not large. Not especially welcoming.

districts.name: The Gables
districts.description: Upper-middle-class Dunmore — comfortable homes, respectable streets, the kind of neighborhood where people have opinions about property values and worry about what the pamphlets are doing to them.

districts.name: Market District
districts.description: The commercial spine of Dunmore. Shops, stalls, inns, and temples crowd the road intersections. It is loud, busy, and currently angry — pamphlets change hands between purchases.

districts.name: The Warrens
districts.description: The oldest, densest part of Dunmore. Narrow streets, proud heritage, and the working class that built this city and has been watching its anger be aimed somewhere convenient.

initial.description: The seat of Dunmore's local government, anchoring the roundabout plaza at the civic quarter's center. Guards are posted. Officials move with the harried look of people managing a city on edge. Traffic here has increased markedly in recent days.

explored.description: Concord operatives have been observed using a side entrance — the one reserved for messengers and minor officials. Someone inside is either working with them or is being used without knowing it.

fully_explored.description: The town hall has served as a node in the Concord's information network. Operatives monitored the local political response to the propaganda campaign from here — tracking whether the manufactured crisis was producing the intended effect.

secrets.text: At least one official here has been receiving payments. The source traces back to the same organization funding the printing operation.
Cael Darro used this building's messenger network to position himself in Dunmore before the party arrived. The coincidence of his appearance was arranged weeks in advance.

initial.description: One of the larger private estates in the High Quarter. The household holds frequent gatherings — wine, debate, the usual performance of influence. The kind of place where Dunmore's opinion-makers tell each other what to think.

explored.description: Mirelle Voss has been a fixture at these gatherings for the past month, moving through the social circles that shape the city's political response. She is better connected than she has any obvious reason to be.

fully_explored.description: Mirelle used Haverstock's network to map Dunmore's landscape of influence — identifying who could be bought, who could be managed, and who would look away. Her time here was an assessment operation, not socializing.

secrets.text: Mirelle attended as 'Sera Vantalle', a merchant's widow from the southern provinces. The alias is clean and well-constructed.
It was Mirelle who identified the party as useful after the convoy incident and arranged for Cael Darro to be here when they arrived. The Concord's apparent coincidence was her design.

initial.description: A well-maintained temple to the goddess of civilization and law, attended primarily by merchants, civic officials, and the upper-middle class of the Gables. The clergy are aligned with Dunmore's sense of its own importance and heritage. Services are formal. Donations are visible.

explored.description: The head priest, Brother Aldric Vane, has been conspicuously quiet about the propaganda. He preaches order — but order, the party may note, does not require asking where the pamphlets come from.

fully_explored.description: Brother Vane received a quiet donation three months ago from a civic 'beautification fund' that does not appear in any public record. He has not asked questions. Erathis teaches that civilization requires pragmatism.

secrets.text: The donation was Concord money. Brother Vane's silence on the propaganda was purchased — not cheaply, and not without his understanding what he was agreeing to.

initial.description: A respected haberdasher serving the Gables and upper market trade. Hats, caps, scarves, gloves, and fine small wares — the kind of shop where you can spend an hour selecting a belt buckle. Currently doing brisk business in hats with brims large enough to obscure a face.

explored.description: Old Barrow notices everything and forgets nothing. He has seen faces come and go from the civic quarter that don't belong to any household he recognizes. He will talk, if asked carefully and treated well.

initial.description: A modest but busy shrine to the goddess of luck, change, and travel, tucked into a corner of the market district where merchants and travelers pass by. Coins are left at the feet of her icon — the trickster-goddess of good fortune. Travelers pray here before the road. Gamblers pray here before everything.

explored.description: The shrine's keeper, a cheerful woman named Tessaly, has a talent for hearing things. She is not a gossip — but she remembers what she's told in confidence, and distinguishes carefully between information and secrets.

initial.description: A dense cluster of food carts and open-air stalls occupying the widest intersection in the market district. Bread, roasted meats, pies, pickled vegetables, spiced nuts, cheap wine. It is loud, fragrant, and currently serving as an informal distribution point for anti-Elkenquay pamphlets — left on cart edges, pressed into hands with purchases.

explored.description: The cart owners did not choose to distribute the pamphlets. They appeared one morning, already stacked and ready. No one saw who left them. None of the vendors will admit to having passed them on, but none will deny it either.

initial.description: The most popular tavern in the market district. Loud, full, and running about thirty percent angrier than usual. Pamphlets pass between tables. The barkeep keeps his opinions to himself, which is its own kind of opinion.

explored.description: Cael Darro has been seen here regularly — losing at cards with good grace, buying rounds, listening carefully. He fits in too well. He has been here before the party arrived.

fully_explored.description: The Crossed Keys was Cael Darro's primary observation post in Dunmore. He used the tavern's noise as cover. The barkeep has been paid to be incurious about the corner table.

secrets.text: Cael's regular table has sightlines to both doors. He has been coming here since before the party arrived in Dunmore.

initial.description: Dunmore's dedicated bookseller — maps, histories, religious texts, fiction of uncertain quality, and a back shelf of books the proprietor will show you only if you ask specifically. Mira, the proprietor, has ink-stained fingers and an excellent memory for which customers buy which kinds of books.

explored.description: Mira has noticed that someone has been buying up every map of the greater Dunmore region she can source. She has been asked not to discuss it and has been offered coin to ensure her discretion. She declines to say by whom — but she will confirm that it was not a local.

secrets.text: The regional maps were purchased by a Concord operative. The Concord has been mapping movement corridors in the area for months — the propaganda is one instrument of a much larger operation.

initial.description: A working tailor serving the middle market — repairs, alterations, and commissions for people who want to look presentable without spending noble money. Currently backed up two weeks on orders. Half the city apparently decided this was a good moment to have something fitted.

A reliable smithy at the market district's western edge — tools, hardware, horseshoes, basic weapons, and repair work. Tam Ashford keeps short hours and long prices, but his work holds. He has been quietly turning down orders for anything longer than a short sword and won't say why.

explored.description: Tam has heard things at the forge — men talking while they wait for work, the kind of conversation people have when they think a fire drowns out their voices. He's been turning down weapons orders because he doesn't want to know what they're for.

initial.description: A small apothecary on an unnamed side-street in the Warrens — no sign except a single grey vial hung above the door. Stocks healing potions, basic alchemical components, and a modest selection of wands. The proprietor, Orvyn, is polite, unhurried, and asks no questions. His prices are fair. His sourcing is not discussed.

explored.description: Orvyn maintains a secondary stock not displayed on shelves — substances that are legal in some jurisdictions, components that have legitimate uses if you don't ask what those uses are. He will share this stock with customers he trusts, which takes more than one visit to become.

fully_explored.description: Orvyn has had at least one Concord contact as a regular customer in recent months. What they purchased and why is not something he has volunteered. He is careful. He is also, it appears, still alive — which suggests the Concord considers him useful rather than a liability.

secrets.text: Orvyn supplied components to the printing operation — not the paper, but the alchemical compounds used to treat it, making it resistant to water damage and easier to mass-produce. He knew what it was for.

initial.description: A small chapel to the god of life and healing, wedged between a tanner and a boarding house in the Warrens. The priest, Sister Hadara, runs on donations and determination. Healing is available to anyone who needs it; the suggested offering is whatever you can spare. The chapel smells of tallow candles and dried herbs.

explored.description: Sister Hadara has been treating more injuries than usual — men who won't say what happened, women with bruises from arguments that escalated. The tension in the Warrens is producing its own damage. She is angry about it, quietly, in the way of someone who has to stay functional.

initial.description: An old building on a back street of the Warrens. The windows are covered. There is a faint smell of ink. Locals say it has been vacant for years, though the door latch shows fresh wear.

explored.description: The source of the anti-Elkenquay propaganda. The operation inside is organized — multiple press runs, a coordinated distribution network, messaging that has been carefully targeted by someone who understands how to make people angry at a specific thing. This is not amateur agitation.

fully_explored.description: The printing operation is a Concord instrument. The pamphlets are part of a manufactured crisis — Elkenquay sentiment has been strategically inflamed to create the political conditions the Concord requires. A resonance artifact was stored here, likely used to power equipment.

secrets.text: The operation's paper supply was routed through a warehouse in the lower market. The funding traces through three intermediaries, each using the same courier.
The Concord runs this operation. The propaganda campaign is an instrument of a much larger strategy — one that requires a destabilized region and a population primed to welcome order when it arrives.

explored.description: A respectable lodging house in the Warrens. Chaelynn has been staying here — a familiar face, the long-lost contact the party trusts. Her presence in Dunmore feels like a coincidence. It is not.

fully_explored.description: Chaelynn has been observing the party throughout the Prologue and reporting to Cael Darro. Her placement in Dunmore was deliberate — she was positioned to provide a trusted face at the moment of Concord recruitment. Whether her care for the party is genuine and her mission is separate from that, or whether they were always the same thing, is a question the skill leaves open.

secrets.text: A letter in Chaelynn's room, if found, is in cipher. It is addressed to 'C.D.' How much of her friendship with the party has been a Concord instrument is deliberately left unanswered.

explored.description: An old civic gatehouse at the boundary of the civic quarter and the market district. Used by the city watch as a patrol staging post. After the monstrosity attack, this is where the Concord extracted the party.

fully_explored.description: The extraction point was pre-selected. Cael Darro knew in advance where the attack would drive the crowd — and positioned his team accordingly. The rescue was not reactive. It was choreographed.

secrets.text: Chaelynn was already at the gatehouse when the party arrived. She had been positioned there before the monstrosity was released. She knew it was coming.
